title: Infinitely Many Primitive Odd Abundant Numbers

problemStatement.formal: \left\{\, n \in \mathbb{N} \;\middle|\; \text{Odd } n \;\wedge\; \sigma(n) > 2n \;\wedge\; \forall\, d \mid n,\ d < n \Rightarrow \sigma(d) < 2d \,\right\}\ \text{is infinite.}
problemStatement.plain: An abundant number has proper divisors summing to more than itself (smallest is 12; smallest odd one is 945 = 3^3*5*7). It is primitive abundant if it is abundant but no proper divisor of it is. The parent entry proved infinitely many odd abundant numbers via 945*(2k+1), but every such witness is a multiple of the abundant 945, so none is primitive. This problem asks the harder question: are there infinitely many primitive odd abundant numbers? A new infinite family of odd witnesses is needed, where abundance appears for the first time exactly at the witness.
whyMatters: Primitive abundant numbers generate all abundant numbers under divisibility, so understanding the primitive ones controls the entire set.
The even primitive abundant numbers are known to be infinite (via 2^k*p and Bertrand), but that construction is fundamentally even; the odd case is far more delicate because odd abundance is rare.
Formalizing this closes the last and hardest open question recorded in the abundant-number-oq-03 gallery entry, sharpening the separation between rarity and structural minimality.

proven: infinitely_many_odd_abundant: there are infinitely many odd abundant numbers, via the non-primitive family 945*(2k+1) (entry abundant-number-oq-03).
abundant_945: 945 is abundant, proved axiom-free by kernel decide (entry abundant-number-oq-02).
Infinitely many (even) primitive abundant numbers via 2^k*p with a prime p in the window 2^k-1 < p < 2^(k+1)-1 (entry abundant-number-oq-01-oq-04).
abundant_mul_right: closure of abundant numbers under positive multiples (entry abundant-number-oq-01).
open: Whether there are infinitely many primitive odd abundant numbers: 945*(2k+1) is odd but never primitive, and 2^k*p is primitive but never odd, so neither known construction settles it.
An explicit infinite family of odd numbers that are abundant with all proper divisors deficient is not currently in Mathlib or the gallery.
knownResults.goal: Formalize {n | Odd n and IsPrimitiveAbundant n}.Infinite in Lean 4 / Mathlib, exhibiting a concrete infinite family of odd primitive abundant witnesses with proofs that each is odd, abundant, and has every proper divisor deficient.
